QuestionStmt.S: The area of the region bounded by $$\frac{x^2}{9} + \frac{y^2}{4} = 1$$ and the line $$\frac{x}{3} + \frac{y}{2} = 1$$ is

Solution.S:
Required area = A(OACB) - A(△OAB)

Given equation of ellipse is $\frac{x^2}{9} + \frac{y^2}{4} = 1$

$$\frac{y^2}{4} = 1 - \frac{x^2}{9}$$

$$y = \frac{2}{3} \sqrt{9 - x^2}$$

A(OACB) = $$\int_0^3 \frac{2}{3} \sqrt{9 - x^2} \, dx$$

$$= \frac{2}{3} \left[ \frac{1}{2} x \sqrt{9 - x^2} + \frac{9}{2} \sin^{-1} \frac{x}{3} \right]_0^3$$

$$= \frac{2}{3} \left[ \frac{1}{2} \cdot 3 \sqrt{9 - 9} + \frac{9}{2} \sin^{-1} 1 - \frac{1}{2} \cdot 0 \sqrt{9 - 0} - \frac{9}{2} \sin^{-1} 0 \right]$$

$$= \frac{2}{3} \cdot \frac{9}{2} \cdot \frac{\pi}{2} = \frac{3\pi}{2}$$

A(△OAB) = $$\frac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 2 = 3$$

Required area = $$\frac{3\pi}{2} - 3 = \frac{3}{2} (\pi - 2) \text{ sq. units}$$

Alternate method:

The area between $\frac{x^2}{a^2} + \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1$ and straight line $\frac{x}{a} + \frac{y}{b} = 1$ is $\frac{1}{4} \pi ab - \frac{1}{2} ab$ sq. units.

Required area = $$\frac{1}{4} \pi (3)(2) - \frac{1}{2} (3)(2) = \frac{3}{2} (\pi - 2) \text{ sq. units}$$

Hence the correct option is B.
